subject: general
question: Atul’s salary is ₹10,000 per month. He spends ₹6,000 on house rent and ₹2,500 on bills, and the rest of the amount is his monthly savings. Find his savings (in ₹) in a year, if in the month of his birthday, he spent all his monthly savings on birthday celebrations.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Monthly Salary = 10,000

Monthly Expenditure = 6,000 + 2,500 = 8,500

Monthly Savings = 10,000 − 8,500 = 1,500

Yearly Savings (excluding birthday month) = 1,500 × 11 = 16,500

**∴ The correct answer is ₹16,500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Monthly Salary** = ₹10,000

**House Rent** = ₹6,000

**Bills** = ₹2,500

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8b81a4e24003d89911a4210530f3de5f23c924c508dd141ccb9280c3f0fb753a.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Total Monthly Expenses** = 6,000 + 2,500 = ₹8,500

⇒ **Monthly Savings** = 10,000 − 8,500 = ₹1,500

⇒ Since he spends his savings in the **birthday month**, he only saves for **11 months**.

⇒ **Yearly Savings** = 1,500 × 11

⇒ **Yearly Savings** = ₹16,500

**∴ The correct answer is ₹16,500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Savings Formula

Basic relation: Savings = Income − Expenditure. Net annual savings is the sum of savings across all 12 months.

Percentage Change in Savings

If income increases by x% and expenditure increases by y%, the new savings are calculated using the updated values of both.
